summary.headline: Anand Rathi Wealth H1 FY27 PAT rose about 23% YoY to INR 238 crore; Q2 net mobilisation hit a record INR 4,186 crore, up 39%.
summary.overview:
Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated net profit of INR 122 crore (up 22% YoY) on revenue of INR 357 crore (up 16%), with adjusted H1 PAT of INR 238 crore (up about 23%) on revenue of INR 693 crore (up 17%). Adjusted figures exclude fair value gains, ESOP expenses and related tax effects. H1 delivered 49% of the INR 1,415 crore revenue guidance and 52% of the INR 460 crore PAT guidance. Net flows, equity mutual fund flows and client acquisition were at or near record levels, while AUM was pressured by a weak Nifty quarter. An interim dividend of INR 4 per share was declared post-bonus.</overview>

segments.name: Private wealth (flagship)
segments.commentary: Client families reached 14,309 after 1,500 net additions in 12 months. AUM-based client attrition was 0.17% in Q2 and 0.26% in H1. Q2 flows split 62% existing clients and 38% new clients.

segments.name: Digital wealth (B2B2C)
segments.commentary: AUM grew 14% YoY to INR 2,531 crore; clients rose 15% YoY to 7,584.

segments.name: OFA (SaaS platform)
segments.commentary: About 6,898 subscribers with platform assets of about INR 1.66 lakh crore at end-September 2026; management noted these are platform assets only.

segments.name: Structured products (MLDs)
segments.commentary: Q2 primary MLD issuance was about INR 2,073 crore and secondary about INR 750 crore. Management said MLD growth of 20-25% is the near-term expectation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance INR 1,415 crore (49% achieved in H1); FY27 PAT guidance INR 460 crore (52% achieved in H1).

FY27 AUM target INR 1.2 lakh crore; net flow target of INR 6,000-8,000 crore for the balance of the year, per the Q&A, with management saying flows of about INR 3,000-4,000 crore per quarter for the next two quarters is the aim.
Management expects ESOP cost to fall sharply next year as the grant-year charge declines.
PBT margin target about 40% and PAT margin above 30%, with excess profit reinvested in technology and verticals.
GIFT City entity: two funds expected to launch within about 2-3 months; no revenue provisioned in FY27 guidance.
Mutual fund licence application to be filed by month-end October 2026.
capex_capacity: 431 relationship managers with capacity to handle about 8,000 more client families, per management.
About 900 account managers and RMs in the delivery engine; 500 account managers in the pipeline, with the next 100 RMs being trained for promotion over 1-1.5 years.
182 research staff focused on delivering 5-6% Jensen's alpha to clients.
London operations started last quarter; GIFT City regulatory approvals received, with an in-principle IFSCA approval in July 2026.
Mutual fund licence application (AMC inside the group) planned for filing by end-October 2026.
demand_pricing: Q2 net mobilisation was a record INR 4,186 crore; equity mutual fund net flow was a record INR 2,867 crore (+39% YoY). SIP flows were robust and lump-sum flows were low.
AUM was INR 1.08 lakh crore (+18% YoY). Q2 mark-to-market was about minus INR 2,000 crore; management said Nifty fell about 5% in the quarter.
Management said it does not discount fees for larger clients; fee rates for the top UHNI tier are the same or marginally better than for the 5-50 crore segment.
Management said the 14,000+ client base has a potential of more than INR 1 lakh crore in wallet, and it targets 50-70% of wallet share with platinum clients.
Management said its flows are about 60-70% from existing clients, and clients are onboarded starting at INR 1 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise sharply after ESOP grants, and will ESOP cost decline next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap between PBT of INR 122 crore and the INR 90 crore base will narrow as non-cash ESOP and mark-to-market charges reduce, and that ESOP cost will fall dramatically next year.

qa_highlights.question: How big are non-cash charges in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-cash charges (ESOP and mark-to-market) were INR 46 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with zero in the same quarter last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of net flows between existing and new clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 flows were 62% from existing clients and 38% from new clients, and management typically sees 60-70% from existing clients.

qa_highlights.question: What are the primary and secondary MLD issuances in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Primary issuance was about INR 2,073 crore and secondary was about INR 750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are AUM and flow targets if market volatility rises?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM target is INR 1.2 lakh crore for the year. Flows of INR 3,000-4,000 crore per quarter are the aim for the next two quarters; AUM is the most volatile guidance because it is measured on a single day.

qa_highlights.question: Will SEBI allowing PMS platforms to offer mutual fund advisory be competitive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a competitive threat, arguing that mutual funds are transacted rarely and that PMS-based fee structures suit RIAs more than MF investors.

risks_watch: AUM and flow guidance are sensitive to market levels; a 2-3% mark-to-market move changes AUM materially, per management.
Mark-to-market losses and ESOP charges (INR 46 crore in Q2 vs zero last year) are dampening reported profit; watch the reduction in non-cash charges.
MLD product returns: some products delivered 6-7% rather than the 14-15% target in the falling market; management said no product has lost money at maturity.
Management said new-client sentiment is weaker in a falling market, as clients expected 10-15% returns and are seeing 2-3%.
GIFT City and mutual fund licence are unproven and carry execution risk; no revenue has been provisioned for GIFT City in FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and client outcomes, with an emphasis on consistency and long-term discipline. Management was candid about weak recent returns and the AUM shortfall from market mark-to-market. Some answers were long and informal, and the call had audio disruption, but no material financial question was avoided.
